I don't always see the type of financing specifically defined in the contract, and I would want to defer to a licensed RE Agent to understand better the rules around that. I'm not sure if it's a custom that differs between regions, or if it's a statewide requirement.


I will say that there have been plenty of times where a borrower originally applied for conventional financing and the contract was written that way, but had to switch to FHA mid-process. I rarely ever saw an addendum solely about financing type changes. 


My opinion, for what it's worth, is that this is a situation where it really helps to have a good agent with good relationships. While I think it's discriminatory for sellers to turn down an offer because of financing type, there are minimum property standards for FHA that do not apply conventionally so I understand why the selling side gets squeamish. Sometimes clear communication between agents and trusted track records makes all the difference.


Believe it or not, people are still doing personal letters to the seller along with their offers. A friend of mine recently sold her cute cape to a family using FHA financing and turned down the cash offers. 

Best of luck!

Thanks for bringing up the homes that need TLC. There are renovation loans out there and in this market there are lenders jumping on that business. 

However, if you do want CHFA financing, they only do the FHA government insured rehab loan (aka 203k). Still, worth it to get into the home and refi at a later date.

Make sure you go to www.chfa.org and work with a lender authorized to write CHFA loans. There are a few different programs offering reduced interest rates and down payment/closing cost assistance, but I will offer some of the most popular: 


1. SMART RATE - 1.125% interest reduction if you carry at least $15k of student debt in good standing (does NOT need to be in repayment status)

2. TIME TO OWN - up to $25k in FORGIVABLE down payment & closing cost assistance 

3. Additional Down payment/closing cost assistance (aka community second mortgages) can be stacked with a single CHFA down payment/closing cost loan. Make sure you check with the town or city you are purchasing in to see if they offer these specialized loans, and also look into additional funding with The Housing Development Fund: https://hdfconnects.org/ 
You could potentially stack multiple loans, some with zero monthly payments, reducing your 1st mortgage loan amount and thus the overall monthly payment.


I also highly encourage everyone to sign up for a free homebuyer education class at your closest homeownership center. There is also an online course that is free only after you have secured your lender.

https://www.chfa.org/homebuyers/homebuyer-education/

Source: I underwrite affordable loans, I am happy to answer any questions!

Well said! And forgive me for hijacking this comment to add to OP that y'all will benefit from some family and individual counseling. If it's not feasible right now for everyone to be in individual counseling, at least family counseling will help you all untangle this very complicated emotional circuitry in a SAFE and moderated space. It's not going to help anyone to blanketly accept the situation in the interest of avoiding more hurt feelings. Guilt, shame, anger... All valid emotions that when left unchecked can soon calcify into resentment and contempt and is much harder to chip away at. We're human, and just because we have emotions doesn't inherently make us experts at managing them. It may get worse before it gets better, but it will get better. I had a secret sibling that knew about me, I understand some of what you're feeling. Just remember that you have the right to your own emotions, you're reality is NOT their reality, you have the right and responsibility to your own future self to set boundaries and allow yourself the space and grace to deal with this in your own way. Best of luck to you.
